blind.description: A stylized historical wheeled plough made primarily of brown timber with dark grey iron fittings. It features a front axle with two small wheels, a sturdy central wooden draft beam, a metal-reinforced plowshare beneath, and two backward-curving wooden guide handles joined by a crossbeam. Surfaces are solid, smooth, and fully textured with hand-painted wood and metal materials.
blind.from_above: An elongated symmetrical tool showing a transverse front axle with two wheels, a straight central beam, and a bifurcated rear handle structure forming a Y-like shape.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 40% as tall as the 5 ft 9 in figure (around 2.3 ft high at the handles) and about 2 ft wide across the wheel axle.
